statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). NQ is quoted at 28,942.25, down 1.51%, and is holding 126 points above the 28,816.25 session low that was set an hour ago. That low has now survived a full hour and the retracement has extended to roughly 43% of the session range, against 19% an hour ago and 3% two hours ago. The three counterweights have all resolved in the same direction: ES has joined the bounce at 19.25 points off its own low, the VIX at 17.59 sits near its 17.48 session low after an 18.17 high, and WTI at 102.54 continues to ease from 103.81. Tail steps down three points to 22 and leaves the block band.
recommendation: Tail at 22 sits in the watch band, below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window has been narrowed to 13:00-16:00 UTC, covering the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first two cash hours, because the current hour no longer carries the structure that placed the two prior hours in the block band. Conditional Tail re-enters the elevated band only across those three hours and peaks at 27, eight points below the strong-block threshold. From 16:00 UTC the conditional path returns to the watch band and reaches the EA_ON mapping across the thinnest Asian hours. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: The 28,816.25 low holds for a full hour and NQ retraces 43% of the session range while ES, the VIX and WTI all come off their extremes; Tail eases to 22 and leaves the block band
body:
The repeated-extension structure that carried the two prior assessments into the block band has now been contradicted by the observed path. NQ is quoted at 28,942.25, down 444.75 points or 1.51% against a 29,387.00 reference, as of 07:15 EDT. The session low is unchanged at 28,816.25, so the sequence of consecutive lower lows has stopped at four, and the contract is trading about 126 points above that low, roughly 43% of the 28,816.25 to 29,111.00 range. An hour ago the same measure was 19% and two hours ago 3%. Tail scores the probability of a path that denies meaningful mean reversion, and a low that has held for a full hour while the bounce extends is direct evidence against that path.

The cross-asset picture has resolved in the same direction. ES at 7,613.00, down 0.61%, is now 19.25 points above its 7,593.75 session low, against 3.75 points an hour ago; the S&P contract was the dissenting signal in the prior assessment and it is no longer dissenting. The VIX at 17.59 is up 11.07% on the day but is trading near its 17.48 session low, with the 18.17 session high unchanged for a second hour, which is decay rather than expansion. WTI at 102.54, up 2.49%, has eased further from its 103.81 high, and Brent is near 107.30. The 10-year is quoted around 4.975% and is not extending, against a 2-year constant maturity of 4.56% at the most recent H.15 publication. The Asian cash sessions have closed, so Monday’s regional reaction to the AI story is complete: the Kospi finished down 3.26% at 6,684.37, SK Hynix down 6.35%, Samsung Electronics down 4.05% and SoftBank down 10.7%.

Both underlying drivers remain unresolved, which is why Tail eases rather than collapses. Anthropic’s chief executive called at the weekend for AI companies to slow the pace at which they advance model capabilities, and the chief executives of OpenAI and xAI said they agreed; premarket quotes put Nvidia below -2% with Intel near -6%, AMD near -5% and Marvell near -6%. On the energy side, Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, which had been carrying roughly 5 million barrels a day, remains shut after drone strikes on 10-11 September, with the Strait of Hormuz closed since March. The Dow-to-Nasdaq spread stays wide, with Dow futures down 0.18% against NQ down 1.51%, which continues to describe a concentrated AI and semiconductor de-rating rather than index-wide liquidation.

Stress stays high at 76 and Confidence at 88. The week still carries Retail Sales and the Fed decision on Wednesday, with roughly 83-86% probability of a hike priced, and event importance under the inherited rule is scored into Stress and Confidence rather than into Tail until a post-event price path is observed. The 13:30 UTC cash open is the remaining checkpoint and is not yet observed, so it is carried in the forecast rather than in the current score. A fresh low beneath 28,816.25 with shallow bounces would restore the one-way reading; a reclaim of 29,000 is the nearest confirmation that the structure has turned two-sided.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available. Tail rose through Sunday’s European and US hours from 13 at 11:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC, eased to 16 at the 16:00 UTC handover, then stepped through 17, 18, 18 and 19 into the Globex reopen, crossing into the watch band at 21 and peaking at 22 in the reopen hour. Across the overnight session it was unusually stable, printing 20 in six of the following eight hours with 19 at 02:00 and 06:00 UTC, before the European open lifted it to 21 at 07:00 UTC, 23 at 08:00 UTC, 26 at 09:00 UTC and 25 at 10:00 UTC, the two hours in the block band. The mapped state was EA_ON and green for the first ten hours, WATCH and yellow for most of the overnight session with two single-hour reversions to green, and BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES with orange for the two most recent hours. Dominant mode read normal through the Sunday hours, event/whipsaw for the reopen hour, mixed from 23:00 UTC onward and trend-down for the two most recent hours. Confidence fell from 86 to 71 around the 16:00 UTC handover, then rebuilt steadily to 88 as live overnight price-path evidence accumulated.
outlookSummary: The danger window has been narrowed from six hours to three and no longer starts at the current hour: it now runs from 13:00 to 16:00 UTC, covering the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first two cash hours. The current hour and the premarket build sit in the watch band at 22 and 23 because the observed retracement has held. Conditional Tail re-enters the elevated band at 26 for the opening-auction hour and peaks at 27 in the first full cash hour, the narrow single-hour top of the series and eight points below the strong-block threshold, before easing to 25 in the second cash hour. That shape reflects a concentrated AI and semiconductor de-rating against a stagflationary energy backdrop rather than index-wide liquidation, and it is carried in the forecast rather than the current score because the opening auction is not yet observed. From 16:00 UTC the conditional path returns to the watch band at 23 and decays through 22 into the 20:00 UTC cash close, with a single tick held at 22 for the power hour. It falls to 20 across the CME maintenance break on a mechanical basis, lifts to 21 at the Globex reopen and 23 for the Tokyo and Seoul opens, where second-day AI sector reaction risk sits, then eases to the EA_ON mapping at 19 through the thinnest Asian hours. It rebuilds to 20, 21, 21 and 22 as Europe reopens on day one of the two-day policy meeting. A fresh low beneath 28,816.25 with shallow pullbacks is the conditional amplifier; a reclaim of 29,000 is the nearest conditional confirmation that structure has turned two-sided.

Whether opening-auction direction persists past the first thirty minutes is the discriminator: repeated extension after failed retracements would justify the level, while a retracement that holds would not.
